notes: All required searches ran this time (8 web searches; none were refused). None returned a statement, bill, letter or hearing remark by Rep. Brendan F. Boyle (D-PA-2) about AI or AI risk; results on superintelligence, extinction, pause, China and 'AI safety' were about other people or general debate. The site:boyle.house.gov search found only his privacy page. From the earlier attempt (kept as still valid): the press release list at https://boyle.house.gov/media-center/press-releases pages 1 to 5 (about 50 releases, 29 January to 9 November 2026) has no title or excerpt mentioning AI; only titles and excerpts were read, not full texts; boyle.house.gov/search returned 403; press releases from 2025 were not checked page by page. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, introduced 24 September 2026): the FastDemocracy bill page (https://fastdemocracy.com/bill-search/us/119/bills/USB00108512/) lists 12 cosponsors and Boyle is not among them; the congress.gov cosponsor page returned 403, so this was not confirmed against the official list, and news reports disagree on the cosponsor list. FastDemocracy and Legiplex profiles tag 'Artificial Intelligence' as a generic issue category but show no AI bill or statement by him. No House letter about AI risk led by him was found (the centrally handled multi-signer letters were not searched, per instructions). Finding nothing here is a search result, not proof he has never spoken about AI.
